fixes.explanation: You've got it, baker. The disciple says, “Lord, first let me go and bury my father.” (Matthew 8:21) Burying his father is the request he makes. Saying goodbye to his family isn't in it, so the statement is false.
Steering isn't what the text says, baker. Matthew 8:24 says the waves engulfed the boat, “But Jesus was sleeping.” The text doesn't say who was steering. It does say who was asleep.

That's the one, baker. The disciples go and wake Him, saying, “Lord, save us! We are perishing!” (Matthew 8:25) They call Him Lord and they ask Him to save them. Jesus' next question, “why are you so afraid?”, shows they were afraid (Matthew 8:26).
Yes, baker. After Jesus rebukes the winds and the sea, “…it was perfectly calm.” (Matthew 8:26) Not a little rough and not mostly calm. PERFECTLY calm.
Offended isn't the word the text gives, baker. “The men were amazed…” (Matthew 8:27). Amazed is their reaction when the violent storm turns perfectly calm.
